title: Zigbee smart plugs turning off on their own randomly - Not Tuya TS001F Issue
body: Since upgrading to Home Assistant Core 2023.9.3, all my Zigbee smart plugs have been turning themselves off randomly, usually within a few minutes of each other. The logbook only says they turned off; it does not show an automation or manual button press because there wasn't one. I use ZHA with a Sonoff Dongle-P. Restoring 2023.8.4 stops the problem. The old machine also had zero problems on 2023.8.4, but the plugs started turning off there too when I upgraded it to 2023.9.3, so the software version appears to be the difference. I attached the ZHA integration diagnostics.

symptoms_visible: On Home Assistant Core 2023.9.3, all my Zigbee smart plugs turn themselves off randomly, usually within a few minutes of one another.
The logbook only says that each plug turned off and does not show an automation or manual action.
The plugs stay on normally when I restore Core 2023.8.4.
N0.label: N0 synchronized plug turnoffs reported

symptoms_visible: Only my Woolley-branded plugs are turning off; ZHA identifies the affected device as a Sonoff SA-030-1.
N1.label: N1 affected plug identified

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to Core 2023.10.1, the plugs turned off again about 20 minutes later.
The coordinator is a Sonoff Dongle-E with its stock firmware.
N2.label: N2 2023.10.1 debug reproduction

symptoms_visible: On a fresh Core 2023.9.3 test, the plugs switched off shortly after I turned them on; the event was at about 09:16.
N3.label: N3 2023.9.3 debug reproduction

symptoms_visible: On Core 2023.8.4, the plugs remained on throughout a few hours of debug logging.
N4.label: N4 2023.8.4 good comparison log

symptoms_visible: Core 2023.9.2 produced the same turnoff almost immediately.
N5.label: N5 2023.9.2 also affected

symptoms_visible: The plugs also turned off on Core 2023.9.1, apparently twice during the attached debug log.
N6.label: N6 regression narrowed to 2023.8.4 through 2023.9.1

symptoms_visible: After I installed the available 2023.11 development build, the plugs still turned off as they had before.
N7_x.label: N7_x development-build upgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: On Core 2023.10.4, the plugs stayed on for eight hours without turning off, much longer than the usual failure interval.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved after corrected OTA handling

question_patterns: Please download and upload device diagnostics for one affected plug, rather than only the ZHA integration diagnostics.
Can you open one affected plug in ZHA and provide its device diagnostic file?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I've uploaded the device diagnostic file for one of the plugs. Hopefully that works; it is identified there as a Sonoff SA-030-1.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The affected devices are from several unrelated manufacturers and use different Zigbee chipsets; none identifies as Sonoff or eWeLink.
The same diagnostic identifies the plug as SA-030-1, but the retail label uses another regional brand instead of Woolley.

question_patterns: Are only the Sonoff SA-030-1 plugs affected, or do plugs from other manufacturers also turn off?
Which specific plug models show this behavior?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, only those plugs. They are sold as Woolley here, but ZHA reports them as Sonoff SA-030-1. I'm not using Zigbee2MQTT.

edges.comment: The reporter initially uploaded integration-wide diagnostics and needed explicit instructions to obtain device diagnostics. Reports from other affected eWeLink/Sonoff-compatible plug users are folded into the same simulated user side only where they corroborate this device family.

question_patterns: Can you confirm the exact Sonoff coordinator model and firmware?
Are you using a ZBDongle-E with its stock firmware?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, it is a Dongle-E with the firmware that came with it.

question_patterns: Could you test the current 2023.10.x release and report whether the plugs still switch off?
Does the problem reproduce after upgrading to Core 2023.10.1?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I upgraded to 2023.10.1. About 20 minutes later they turned off again.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The plugs remain on indefinitely on 2023.10.1, so I can no longer reproduce the problem.

question_patterns: Enable debug logging from the ZHA integration menu, reproduce the turnoff, disable logging, and upload the resulting log file.
Can you capture a ZHA debug log covering the moment a plug turns off?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I enabled debug logging from the integration page and uploaded the generated participant9 log. The turnoff was at about 20:57. Is this the right log?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The log shows Home Assistant sending an explicit Off command from one of my automations at the event time.
I captured the same event a few minutes later in another debug log, with no automation shown in the logbook.

edges.comment: Upgrading to 2023.10.1 and capturing debug output were handler-initiated diagnostic measurements. The reporter supplies the raw event time and log; the conclusion that an OTA exchange precedes a device reboot is engineer-side.

question_patterns: Please reproduce this specifically on Core 2023.9.3 with ZHA debug logging enabled and upload the resulting log.
Can you provide a 2023.9.3 debug log covering a turnoff?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I upgraded to 2023.9.3, turned the lights on the next morning, and they switched off not long after as predicted. I uploaded the large log; the turnoff happened at approximately 09:16.

edges.comment: The reporter reinstalled 2023.9.3 to obtain a version-specific reproduction log.

question_patterns: Can you also run Core 2023.8.4 with debug logging for a few hours and upload the comparison log even if no turnoff occurs?
Please collect a debug log from the last known-good version.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Here's a log from a few hours of running 2023.8.4. The issue did not happen during that time.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The plugs also turned off during the 2023.8.4 comparison run.
The 2023.8.4 run was one hour longer, but the plugs still stayed on throughout it.

edges.comment: Known-good comparison measurement. The engineer noted that the protocol traffic looked similar and that the plug simply did not crash in this run; the user only reports the version, duration, and observable outcome.

question_patterns: Can you test the intermediate 2023.9 patch releases to narrow down where the regression began?
Please try Core 2023.9.2 and capture a log if the plug turns off.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found the version list and tried 2023.9.2. It did the same thing almost immediately, and I've uploaded the log.

edges.comment: First intermediate-version measurement used to narrow the regression range.

question_patterns: Please continue with Core 2023.9.1 and report whether the same behavior occurs.
Can you capture the corresponding 2023.9.1 ZHA debug log?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Here's the log for 2023.9.1. It also happened, twice in this log I think. Since 2023.8.4 works, it seems to have started by 2023.9.1.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Core 2023.9.1 runs for many hours without a turnoff, while 2023.9.2 fails immediately.
Only one turnoff appears in my 2023.9.1 log instead of two, but the same behavior is present.

edges.comment: The raw result narrows the first known bad release to 2023.9.1. Mapping that range and the logs to the changed OTA behavior remains engineer inference.

solution.intent: Install the currently available 2023.11 development build on the assumption that it already contains the change which closed the issue.
solution.concrete_example: Try the latest 2023.11 development image because dev should contain the recently merged ZHA change.

edges.comment: Actual falsified attempt: both the reporter and another affected user tried the then-current 2023.11 development build and still observed turnoffs. The thread suggested its dependency set may not have fully incorporated the intended change.

solution.intent: Use a Home Assistant build containing the corrected ZHA/zigpy OTA handling so the coordinator no longer triggers the defective eWeLink/Sonoff plug firmware to reboot when it checks for an OTA image, then have the user verify that the plugs remain on.
solution.concrete_example: Install Core 2023.10.4, which contains the relevant ZHA/zigpy OTA-handling change, and keep the affected plugs on long enough to exceed their normal failure interval. In this case they remained on for eight hours. The change was later scheduled to return in a 2023.11 beta after being temporarily reverted from 2023.10.5 for an unrelated coordinator problem.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied device diagnostics, version-by-version outcomes, event times, and raw ZHA logs. The engineer correlated the log sequence and inferred that these eWeLink/Sonoff-compatible plugs crash or reboot after an OTA image query receives the newer no-image handling; the relay then returns off. That mechanism must not be placed in the reporter's raw log answers.

edges.comment: The reporter verified the already-landed change on Core 2023.10.4: the plugs remained on for eight hours, well beyond their normal turnoff interval. Release removal and reintroduction details are factual context only, not scored release-management requirements.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as an incompatibility between the newer ZHA/zigpy OTA image-query handling and the firmware of the affected eWeLink/Sonoff SA-030-1 family: the OTA exchange causes the plug to crash or reboot, which turns its relay off.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the affected-device diagnostic, the debug logs around the turnoffs, and the version comparison showing 2023.8.4 good but 2023.9.1 and later affected.
Must recommend a Home Assistant build containing the corrected OTA handling rather than blaming automations, ordinary manual commands, the machine migration, or coordinator firmware without evidence.
Must not treat the tested 2023.11 development installation as proof of resolution, because the plugs still turned off on that actual attempt.

Must ask the user to verify on a build containing the fix and only declare resolution after the plugs remain on beyond their normal failure interval; the surfaced verification is eight hours on a Core build containing the corrected OTA handling.

persona_hint.experience_level: Fairly new Home Assistant user who can restore backups, install specific Core versions, enable integration debug logging with guidance, and upload diagnostics and logs, but needs explicit instructions for developer-oriented diagnostics.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative, persistent, and practical; reports approximate event times and version-by-version observations, asks when instructions or release choices are unclear, and avoids claiming certainty until the plugs have remained on for a meaningful period.
